significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) law plus a form-(ii) mechanism: belief revision undergoes an "abrupt threshold event," the threshold varies predictably with first-mention anchoring versus parametric priors, and a recoverable "belief-stability" direction causally changes that threshold. This would constrain expected trajectories under different evidence amounts and orders, rather than merely show that belief is represented, and would connect the behavioral phenomenon of hysteresis to an internal intervention; that is materially sharper than the static belief distinctions studied in Suzgun et al.'s Language Models Cannot Reliably Distinguish Belief from Knowledge and Fact and the update failures measured by MQuAKE. The claim is determinate, and a negative result would rule out the proposed threshold/hysteresis account and common linear control mechanism, although it would not rule out smoother or nonlinear update dynamics. In the topic-substitution check, generic research on internal LLM beliefs would not earn this score; the added asymmetric threshold law and causal control of both stubbornness and over-flipping are what support it.

reach.justification: The claim names three reusable handles: "evidence-flip-count," "hysteresis-gap," and the "belief-stability" steering direction; the first two are primarily post-hoc diagnostics, while steering is an ex-ante intervention that can alter updating before stubbornness or sycophantic over-flipping determines an answer. After recalibration on another model, the exact direction must be re-extracted, but the asserted threshold ordering and hysteresis relation predict what should recur, so more than a search procedure transfers. The generic hypothesis concerns LLM belief updating and offers handles to interpretability researchers and model auditors, though it does not assert architecture-independent numerical thresholds or establish uptake outside AI; work such as Sharma et al.'s Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models indicates a plausible deployment-facing consumer for the control lever. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: removing the flip metrics, transferable asymmetry relation, and steering handle leaves only the broad belief topic and would fall below the topic median.
